testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When checking tire condition during a vehicle inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: The insides of the tires are more worn than the outsides.
The outsides of the tires are more worn than the insides.
The middles of the tires are more worn than the outsides.
The tires have even wear across the whole surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires have even wear across the whole surface.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, your tire treads should be worn evenly.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip tire inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread depth of 2/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: When inspecting tires, check that front tires have at least 4/32 of an inch tread depth and other tires have at least 2/32 of an inch. Tires must not be worn, cracked, or under-inflated. All tires must be the same size. Tires from different makers are acceptable.

questions.question: What is true about a suspension system?

options.text: It has a weight capacity rating.
It uses pressurized water to hold the load.
It can handle any weight load.
It has a minimum weight rating.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has a weight capacity rating.
questions.explanation: Manufacturers give suspension systems a weight capacity rating.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce brake use. The four types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: When you need to make an emergency stop, what should you do?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Stop while keeping your vehicle in a straight line.
Expect your vehicle to stop faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop while keeping your vehicle in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking to keep your vehicle in a straight line while still being able to turn if needed.

questions.question: If there is fog on the roadway, what is best for you to do?
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is always dangerous. Avoid driving in foggy conditions whenever possible.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel while driving?

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides.

questions.question: Is it good to look far ahead while driving?

options.text: No, because you cannot do much about something far ahead.
Yes, it helps you see hazards early.
Yes, only if you are transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps you see hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot hazards and respond safely.

questions.question: When entering a foggy area, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: When entering fog, slow down. Use low beam headlights. Do not pass other vehicles or stop on the roadway. The safest choice is to avoid driving in fog.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the vehicle and try to restart it.
Exit the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
Try to flag down another vehicle for help.
Wait in the vehicle for a police officer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If stuck on railroad tracks, get out immediately and walk away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs or signal boxes, then call that number or 911.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This will slow your vehicle and help it regain grip on the road.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Shoes with oil or grease on them
Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: Signs of brake problems include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are worn very thin, broken, or missing.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand so you can eat or drink.
With one hand at a time, switching hands.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Your hands should be on opposite sides of the wheel to maintain control.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, which should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: If you lose brake pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Find a safe place to stop, like an escape ramp, open field, or side street. Do not speed up.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, what should a driver do?
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When should oil pressure reach a normal level after starting the engine?
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, watch the gauges. Oil pressure should reach a normal level within a few seconds.

questions.question: What can the air in air storage tanks contain?
questions.explanation: Air in storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brake system, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop after a short distance?

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire tread is good.
Make sure you changed the right tire.
Check if rocks are in the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short while later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: When should parking brakes be tested?

options.text: Only after you have driven some distance.

questions.explanation: Always test your parking brakes before driving as part of your pre-trip check. If they do not hold, the vehicle needs to be fixed.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the engine running and in gear.
Use the reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.explanation: To check your lights, set the parking brake, turn off the engine, and remove the key. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out and look at each light to make sure it works.

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Drive straight forward, then back to the right.
Drive straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Drive forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, drive straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must fit completely within the parking space lines.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Increase the space between your car and the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between your car and the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create more space in front of your vehicle. This helps the tailgater pass you safely. Speeding up does not help because the other driver will likely stay close at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles enter the lane you want.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is already in the lane you want.
Do not use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is already in the lane you want.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. If you did not see another vehicle, slow movement gives them time to move or honk to warn you. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, after passing under an overpass, your examiner may ask you to remember:

options.text: If there was a shoulder near the road.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, your examiner may ask you about the posted clearance or height of an overpass you drove under.

questions.question: If you drive a truck that requires a CDL, what is true about seat belts?

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You only need to wear a seat belt if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You only need to wear a seat belt when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: For safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times when operating a truck that requires a CDL.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the correct distance behind the driver.
Keeps a safe distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.
Reduces the weight on the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Damage to the suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: What is the minimum size for hazardous materials placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10 and three-quarter inches square.

questions.question: What is true about a distracted driver?

options.text: They usually react quickly to hazards.
They are usually aware of their surroundings.
They are good drivers to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving causes slower perception, delayed decisions, and poor actions. Watch for distracted drivers and stay away from them when possible.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: When should you turn off your turn signal while making a turn?

options.text: In the middle of the turn.

questions.explanation: Signal early and keep signaling throughout your turn or lane change. Turn off your signal once the turn or lane change is complete.

questions.question: What can happen if your vehicle has a high center of gravity?

options.text: It may get better gas mileage.
It may be hard to see the road.
The tires may not support the weight.

questions.explanation: A high center of gravity makes your vehicle more likely to tip over. This happens when cargo is piled high or heavy items are loaded on top.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing:

options.text: You can usually outrun a train.
Do not rely only on warning signals.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Only check the track closest to your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals.
questions.explanation: Never trust only warning signals at a railroad crossing. Never try to race a train. If there are multiple tracks, check all tracks in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: When checking your brakes, a slack adjuster should move ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than about one inch from where the push rod is attached. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: A 40-foot-long item on a flatbed trailer needs at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. Always use a minimum of two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow instructions.
Refuse to change lanes if you don't want to.

questions.explanation: You will make several lane changes during the driving skills test. Always check traffic and signal before changing lanes. Make smooth, safe lane changes.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly to stay in control. This also gives other drivers time to move out of your way. Always use your turn signal.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, you should check all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check oil level, coolant level and hose condition, power steering fluid, windshield washer fluid, battery connections and fluid, transmission fluid, belt condition, and for leaks or damaged wiring. Do not check fuel level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: If a trailer has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS) but the tractor does not:

options.text: The truck cannot be driven because both need ABS.
Find a different tractor with ABS.
The tractor and trailer can be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor and trailer can be used together.
questions.explanation: Having anti-lock brakes on only the tractor or only the trailer still helps with braking control.

questions.question: What happens when air pressure in the system's air tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.explanation: When air tank pressure drops below 60 psi, a low pressure warning signal activates. This can be a warning light or a wig wag alarm.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Sends air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls when it runs.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for dangers. Plan how you will handle emergencies before they happen.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle only one time during the straight line backing exercise to check its position.

questions.question: Vehicles with dual air brake systems:

options.text: Keep full air pressure in the brakes when the vehicle is off.
Keep some air pressure in the brakes when the vehicle is off.
Must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
Do not need time to build air pressure before a trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, run the engine to build at least 100 psi of air pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within 10 feet of your current position.
Within 1,000 feet of your current position.
Within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the area of road you can see in front of you.

questions.question: When inspecting a vehicle, you must check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt for tightness, cracks, or frays. If any part is not belt-driven, tell the examiner and verify it works properly and is not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: Why drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil. These build up in tanks and can damage the brakes. Drain tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Fuel records for IFTA quarterly tax returns must be kept for:
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicle operators in interstate commerce must register under the International Registration Plan and International Fuel Tax Agreement. Keep mileage and fuel records that support IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns for four years.

questions.question: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle before a trip is:

options.text: To wake up before the drive.

questions.explanation: Inspecting your vehicle before a trip keeps you and others safe. State and federal laws require vehicle inspections before every trip.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
It ensures that the vehicle is inspected regularly.
It makes drivers accountable for inspecting their vehicles.
It provides a plan for the next five trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report informs the motor carrier of issues that affect safe vehicle operation. Fill out a report after each day of driving and note any safety concerns or mechanical problems.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment:

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
The gearshift should be in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, set the parking brake and chock the wheels. Check the engine compartment before getting in the cab and starting the engine.
